studyingInChina.title: Studying in China
studyingInChina.a1: China offers Ministry of Education–listed universities, a growing range of English-taught degrees, affordable tuition and living costs, and generous scholarships — with globally recognised qualifications.
studyingInChina.a2: Yes. Many universities offer full degrees taught entirely in English, especially in medicine, engineering and business. Chinese-taught programs and language foundation options are also available.
studyingInChina.q3: Do I need to speak Chinese?
studyingInChina.a3: Not for English-taught programs. For Chinese-taught programs you may need an HSK qualification; we can advise on a foundation year or language program if needed.
studyingInChina.a4: CAS works with Ministry of Education–listed universities whose degrees are widely recognised. Recognition specifics vary by country and profession, so ask your advisor about your target country.

choosing.title: Choosing a university & program
choosing.q1: How do I choose the right university and program?
choosing.a1: Start with a free study plan — tell us your goal, budget and preferences and a CAS advisor sends you a personalised shortlist. You can also browse and filter universities, programs and scholarships on this site.
choosing.q2: What programs can I apply for?
choosing.a2: Bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees plus non-degree and Chinese-language programs — across fields including medicine (MBBS), engineering, business, computer science and more.
choosing.a3: It means the Ministry of Education has approved the university to enrol international students. CAS focuses on MoE-listed universities, which you can identify by the badge on each university page.

scholarships.title: Scholarships
scholarships.a1: Government (CSC), provincial and university scholarships — both full (tuition, accommodation and a stipend) and partial. Availability varies by university, program and intake.
scholarships.q2: Am I eligible for a scholarship?
scholarships.a2: Eligibility depends on your grades, level, nationality and the specific award. Your CAS advisor matches you to the scholarships you have the best chance of winning.
scholarships.q3: Does CAS help with scholarship applications?
scholarships.a3: Yes — we help you identify suitable scholarships, prepare the documents and submit on time alongside your university application.

applying.title: Applying with CAS
applying.q1: How does the application process work?
applying.a1: Study plan → shortlist → prepare your documents → CAS submits your application → you receive an offer → visa support → arrival support. One team handles the whole journey.
applying.a2: Typically your passport, academic transcripts and certificates, passport photos and, depending on the program, a language certificate and medical or police checks. Your advisor gives you an exact checklist.
applying.a3: It varies by university and intake — often a few weeks to a couple of months from application to offer. Applying early in the intake window gives you the most options.
applying.a4: Yes. Your initial consultation and study plan are free with no obligation. Any paid services are quoted clearly up front — see our pricing page.

visa.title: Visa & arrival
visa.q1: How do I get a student visa?
visa.a1: After you're admitted, the university issues an admission letter and a JW202 form; you then apply for a student (X) visa at a Chinese embassy or consulate. CAS guides you through each step.
visa.q2: Does CAS support me after I arrive?
visa.a2: Yes — airport pickup, help with university registration, accommodation and settling in are part of our end-to-end support.

fees.title: Fees & payments
fees.q1: How much does it cost to study in China?
fees.a1: It depends on the university, city and program — tuition plus living costs. Tell us your plan and we'll give you a clear, personalised estimate.
fees.a2: Your consultation and study plan are free. Where a service has a fee, you'll see an itemised quote before you commit — there are no hidden charges.

mbbs.seoTitle: MBBS in China: Approved Universities & Fees
mbbs.seoDescription: The 43 universities approved by China's Ministry of Education to enrol English-taught MBBS students in 2026–27, with tuition, application windows and how to apply.
mbbs.title: MBBS in China
mbbs.subtitle: The Ministry of Education's approved universities for English-taught MBBS, what you need to apply, and the dates universities have published.
mbbs.how1: China's Ministry of Education publishes an annual list of universities approved to enrol international undergraduate students in English-taught Clinical Medicine (MBBS). For 2026–27 the list has 43 universities. A university that is not on the list may not recruit English-taught MBBS students.
mbbs.how2: Check the list before you apply, and confirm with the licensing council of the country where you plan to practise that a degree from the university is accepted. The programs in our catalog run six years (72 months) and are taught in English; their listed tuition is between CNY 26,000 and CNY 50,000 a year.
mbbs.listSubtitle: Each page shows programs, fees, application windows and scholarships.
requirements: A valid foreign passport; applicants are generally 18 to 25 years old (the exact limit is set by each university).
A high-school diploma, with strong results in biology, chemistry and physics or mathematics.
The China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA) result, which bachelor's applicants take before applying.
Proof of English: IELTS or TOEFL, unless your previous study was taught in English.
A physical examination form and a police clearance certificate, both issued within six months of applying.
A personal statement and, where asked, an online interview with the university.

faq.q: How long is an MBBS in China?
faq.a: The English-taught MBBS programs in our catalog run six years (72 months), and the final year is normally clinical practice.

faq.q: Which universities can enrol international MBBS students?
faq.a: Only universities on the Ministry of Education's annual approved list. For 2026–27 there are 43, all listed on this page.

faq.q: Do I need to speak Chinese?
faq.a: No Chinese is needed to start, because teaching is in English. Universities add Chinese language courses because hospital training involves speaking with patients.
Tuition for the MBBS programs in our catalog is between CNY 26,000 and CNY 50,000 a year, plus accommodation and living costs. Each university page shows its own fees.
It differs by university. Many open in the months before the September intake and close between May and August. Each university page lists the window we have found and how reliable the source is.

mbbs.cta: Not sure which university suits you? A CAS counselor will shortlist for your grades and budget.

csc.seoTitle: CSC Scholarship: Chinese Government Scholarship Guide
csc.seoDescription: How the Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) works: what it covers, who can apply, how to apply and when, and the China-wide scholarships we list.
csc.title: CSC Scholarship
csc.subtitle: What the Chinese Government Scholarship covers, who can apply, and how and when to apply.
csc.what1: The Chinese Government Scholarship, administered by the China Scholarship Council (CSC), funds international students to study at Chinese universities. You apply online through the CSC Study in China system, normally through the Chinese embassy or consulate in your country (using an agency number) or through a host university, and the category and agency number depend on the route you use.
csc.who1: Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens in good health who meet the admission requirements of their target university. In the 2026–27 call published for Canada, age limits were under 25 for bachelor's, under 35 for master's and under 40 for doctoral study. Chinese-taught programs needed HSK 3 (bachelor's) or HSK 4 (master's and doctoral), and bachelor's applicants had to take the CSCA. Other countries' calls can differ.
steps: Choose a university and a program that is listed as open to CSC applicants.
Check your embassy's call: opening dates, deadlines and interview steps differ by country.
Prepare the documents: passport, certified transcripts and diplomas, study plan, recommendation letters and language certificates.
Apply online in the CSC Study in China system and submit the university application, usually with the university's pre-admission notice or invitation letter.
Follow the embassy's or university's instructions for interviews and results.
csc.time1: Dates depend on your country or route. For the 2026–27 round, Chinese embassy notices opened from late October 2025; one embassy opened applications on 16 February 2026, and the 2026–27 call for Canada closed on 22 February 2026. Check your embassy's notice for the current round.
csc.cta: We can match you to CSC-listed programs and help you apply on time.
